title: The Rasen Falcon site and T1/T2
summary: Rasen Falcon static site (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25): under low memory load it should be served from memory. Plan: make a RAM store the size of the site, copy, verify against a digest, switch the root; when RAM is wanted, switch back to the drive and release the store (no flush: nothing was written). T1/T2 (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25): T1 wants fast storage with minimum space on the fabric, T2 more RAM than is free; plan ADD_SWAP 2579 MiB, START T2, START T1; when T2 moves, STOP T2, REMOVE_SWAP, ADD_CACHE T1 5427 MiB WRITEBACK; a later RAM demand flushes and drops that cache first. Caveat: Linux's page cache already keeps a quiet static site in RAM; the explicit store adds a recorded decision, a priority for residency and a ledger entry the arbitrator can reclaim.
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: A read-only store holds the whole data and replaces the root
A cache in front of a drive may hold part of the data (256 MiB at least)
procedure: Use these two as the acceptance cases for any change to the planner
